questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Overcorrect the steering.
Turn your steering wheel toward traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm. Steer the wheel in the same direction the vehicle is skidding.

questions.question: If your car begins to skid out of control, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes gently.
Do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids out of control, do not use the brakes. Keep adjusting your steering until the vehicle is under your control and moving safely.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross safely at marked and unmarked crosswalks. For everyone's safety, give the right-of-way to people crossing any street.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are only for people with disabled parking permits.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
These lanes are reserved for buses and carpool vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are only for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces that are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: Why should drivers watch carefully for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are harder to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers look but do not see motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians. These are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They can move quickly and have less noticeable lights. Always watch for them to prevent crashes.

questions.question: What is the safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down before entering the curve, then speed up as you exit.
Drive at the same speed through the entire curve.
Speed up before entering the curve, then slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve, then speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Gradually increase your speed as you exit. Speeding up while entering a curve makes it hard to control your vehicle.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before you get on the exit ramp.
Slow down after you get on the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower cars on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you get on the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Wait until you are on the exit ramp to slow down. Do not slow down before entering the exit ramp.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Honk at the cars entering the road.
Keep driving at your current speed.
Speed up to avoid slowing traffic.
Change lanes if it is safe to let other cars enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes if it is safe to let other cars enter.
questions.explanation: On roads with two or more lanes, make room for cars entering the road. If the lane next to you is empty, move over to let traffic in.

questions.question: How far back must you stay from a snowplow that has its red or amber lights on?

options.text: 200 feet
300 feet
400 feet
500 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet
questions.explanation: On roads where the speed limit is 35 mph or more, you must stay at least 200 feet behind a working snowplow when its red or amber lights are on.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield when turning left at a green light.
One-way traffic.
Cattle crossing ahead.
Two-way left turn lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield when turning left at a green light.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that when turning left on a green light, you must yield to oncoming traffic and complete the turn only when it is safe.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see at night.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights makes your pupils contract. After the vehicle passes, your pupils need time to adjust back to normal light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for drunk drivers.
Curves ahead.
Slippery when wet.
Apply your brakes quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road surface is slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: When backing up, you should drive at a speed no faster than:

options.text: A slow crawl.
A slow walk.
A jog.
A sprint.

questions.correctAnswerText: A slow walk.
questions.explanation: Back up slowly. Vehicles are harder to control when moving backward.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then enter when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the side of the road. If your vehicle rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Round signs indicate:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you of an upcoming railroad crossing. Use extra caution in these areas.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.
Passing is permitted from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is permitted from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. With one of each, only the side with the broken line can pass.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed everywhere there is present danger.
Tell you what you must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn you of school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black text on white. They show rules you must follow, such as speed limits and parking rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on, you should look toward the ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
Center
Right side
Left side

questions.correctAnswerText: Right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see enough to stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
Your front wheels should be parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the vehicle in park when parking on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels away from the center of the road. If there is a curb, point your wheels toward it when going downhill, or away from it when going uphill.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's weight may make it hard to turn. Reducing speed helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass other vehicles on the left when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When does your vehicle need more distance to stop?

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more stopping distance on wet or icy roads. Loose gravel or stones also increase stopping distance.

questions.question: A car cuts in front of you suddenly. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and press the brake hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you too close, take your foot off the gas. This creates space between you and the other car without hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: You are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and lights on. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle with sirens and lights approaches, continue through the intersection. Then drive to the right and stop. Always give emergency vehicles the right of way.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you are in the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you are in the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane well in advance. Begin slowing down only after you have moved into the exit lane.

questions.question: Highway signs that drivers must obey are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for one hour or more.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain pushes oil from the asphalt to the road surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat brings more oil to the surface.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning in wet conditions?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit used for good weather.
Use your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the road and ride on top of the water. Driving too fast in wet conditions causes this. The best way to prevent hydroplaning is to drive slower in rain than you would in good weather.
